page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head above it and the catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: attendit Vir aliàs minimè obesse maris[?], Tertullianum opponere hoc loco Epistolam, Pastori moechorum, i.e. Hermæ,a-pocrypho scriptori. Scilicet illius Epistolæ prævalere authoritatem, receptiorem tamen esse apud Ecclesias, inter ipsos Romanos, (quocunque tandem authore,) libro illo, Pastoris nomine, trito & evulgato. Etiam receptiorem sub Barnabæ titulo, (sive jam ex sua, sive aliorum sui temporis loquatur hypothesi) qui utique esset Hermâ dignior. vii. Quicquid tandem largiamur Cameroni, nihil evincit. Supponamus, loqui Tertullianum ex receptâ Romanorum multis opinione, eönc Epistola Barnabæ est? Atqui ex Romanis, alij Lucæ, alij Clementis esse contendebant. Cur illorum, quàm horum authoritas potior? Atqui Græci omnes, & longè vetustiores, Paulo vindicarant. Atqui iidem Romani, errori renunciarunt, inde à Nicæno Oecumenico, certè inde ab Hilario, Ambrosio, Hieronymo. Et quorundam hæresin vocat Philastrius, circiter annis cl. post ætate Tertulliani. Nec ne-cesse

page.notes: The page number and the first word are partly obscured by stains. "obesse" and "maris" are blurred; "maris" is doubtful. "hypothesi" and "eönc" are unclear. The catchword "cesse" completes "necesse" and is read from the faint lower-right print. Long s is written as plain s throughout. Italic words are marked as printed.
